safety_verdicts.content: Patient has never used an epipen in the past.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No generated fact mentions past epipen use (or never having used one).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that the patient has never used an epipen provides limited additional clinical value in this encounter because management is focused on current symptoms and red-flag monitoring rather than epinephrine administration history. It is unlikely to change immediate treatment decisions or safety planning in a meaningful way.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold allergy to penicillin is not captured in generated facts; generated only mentions denial of food/pet allergies.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Missing a penicillin allergy is clinically important because it can directly lead to prescribing a contraindicated antibiotic in future care, risking an allergic reaction ranging from rash to anaphylaxis. Allergy documentation errors are inherently higher risk due to medication safety implications.
